title: Return of Stratton Bay's Administration Fee When a Microsoft 365 Subscription Is Cancelled, by ClearPath Relationship
content:
Stratton Bay's license administration fee billed on a cancelled Microsoft 365 Cloud Subscriptions (CSP) subscription is returned according to the client's ClearPath Managed IT Services relationship. Any amount returned is added to the cancellation refund.

- **Returned in full.** The client holds an active ClearPath agreement, and the subscription was purchased fewer than seven calendar days before the cancellation date. The administration fee billed is returned in full.
- **Returned pro rata.** The client holds an active ClearPath agreement, and the subscription was held seven days or more. The return is the administration fee billed, times the calendar days from the cancellation date through the last day of the cycle inclusive, divided by the days in the cycle.
- **Not returned.** The client has no active ClearPath agreement.

**Records read.**

- The administration fee billed is the total of the administration-fee entries on the subscription's billing ledger.
- The purchase moment comes from the subscription record.
- The agreement's status comes from the client's ClearPath Managed IT Services agreement record.

## Judgement table

| Active ClearPath agreement | Calendar days from purchase date to cancellation date | Administration fee returned |
|---|---|---|
| yes | 0 to 6 | all of the fee billed |
| yes | 7 or more | the fee billed, times the days left in the cycle from the cancellation date, divided by the days in the cycle |
| no | any | none |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- An active ClearPath client cancels 5 days after purchase. 30.00 USD of administration fee was billed, and all 30.00 is returned.
- The same client cancels a renewed subscription in its renewal window. 120.00 USD was billed, and 300 of the cycle's 365 days remain. The return is 120.00 times 300, divided by 365, which is 98.63014.
- A client whose ClearPath agreement is under notice, and not active, gets nothing back.
